> I think we would need to expose the stencil buffer as a post-process texture to get ideal results

I did some research when making a stencil demo for 4.5 release page and that's how stencils are usually used in production anyway, there are very few practical things that can be achieved by reading stencils in surface shaders, even the current outline preset that's gonna ship in 4.5 is very limiting because it doesn't really work with hard normals

Depending on whether or not somebody familiar with rendering wants to work on this for 4.6 it might be best to wait for that to be merged first to make sure editor outlines use the best possible implementation that scales well to large selections

>Depending on whether or not somebody familiar with rendering wants to work on this for 4.6 it might be best to wait for that to be merged first to make sure editor outlines use the best possible implementation that scales well to large selections

If it does get sufficiently implemented I wouldn't mind reworking this to use a stencil solution, but otherwise this current solution is pretty contained, and any kind of rework should be relatively painless assuming we have whatever relevant rendering API exposed. 

I can support whatever the decision is.

> > I think we would need to expose the stencil buffer as a post-process texture to get ideal results
> 
> I did some research when making a stencil demo for 4.5 release page and that's how stencils are usually used in production anyway, there are very few practical things that can be achieved by reading stencils in surface shaders, even the current outline preset that's gonna ship in 4.5 is very limiting because it doesn't really work with hard normals

What you are describing is a technique called "software stencils" which is basically just using a regular texture to store arbitrary data. What we expose in Godot 4.5 is "hardware stencils" which are very inflexible, but a lot faster than software stencils. 

What this PR does is implement software stencils using a Viewport and then it does the post processing in a Canvasitem shader. So its actually already doing the technique that you suggest!

We have no plans to expose a readable stencil buffer. But we will eventually support adding custom buffers to the opaque pass which will allow the exact same effects as software stencils (I.e. write to a stencil mask texture during rendering, read from that texture in later passes)

> Depending on whether or not somebody familiar with rendering wants to work on this for 4.6 it might be best to wait for that to be merged first to make sure editor outlines use the best possible implementation that scales well to large selections

This PR should target 4.6 in any case. But (as you can see above) I think the technique is totally fine and doesn't need to wait for any further rendering changes
Works great, but there is an issue with CSGs. Selecting CSG nodes or their parents would display a correct AABB. However, it doesn't work with the selection outline; it ignores CSG geometry.

>However, it doesn't work with the selection outline; it ignores CSG geometry.

Should be fixed.

Also fixed issues with constantly redrawing, resizing or adding viewports, and unnecessary resources.

Documentation done.

Made some other optimizations, not sure what else to do in this regard. I would appreciate feedback from someone with better understanding of Godot's rendering on the implementation, I couldn't find a way around using the two camera/viewport solution without modifying the render pipeline which is not something I'm well versed at yet.

> Made some other optimizations, not sure what else to do in this regard. The outline is updated multiple times per process from different code paths. You can instead make calls to a `_queue_update()`, which ensures `_update_outline()` executes only once per process. You can find examples of `_queue_update()` throughout the codebase. The behavior of the outline is not consistent when I slip the 3D view and select nodes causing different active object per view.

>The outline is updated multiple times per process from different code paths.

The majority of the multiple calls were from updating all the viewports despite them not being visible, so I added some check to resolve this, but the queue update idea did help especially when transforming.

>The behavior of the outline is not consistent when I slip the 3D view and select nodes causing different active object per view.

I couldn't reproduce the mismatching active node after these changes so I suspect it may have been a timing issue due to the multiple calls. Let me know if it's still a problem and I can investigate further.
Can the outline getting part be exposed to scripting? Lots of games use similar outlines for interactable items, and getting them to work by yourself is a massive PITA

>Can the outline getting part be exposed to scripting? 

In this PR probably unlikely, I think that getting this out to the general public for testing within the editor should be the priority before saying its good enough for all use cases, but in general its possible.

It's a similar request to: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/12991, which my opinion is that the 3D editor code is _kind_ of messy and could use a refactor including extracting out parts (like this functionality or the transform gizmo) which could then be used in the in-editor runtime / games in general through scripting.

If we wanted this to work in the in-editor runtime, then this is something that may need to happen eventually which is why it's got a TODO checkbox in the PR post.
Okay, as a follow up PR after testing the feature in editor, works for me ;)

I wonder if it would be a good idea to enable one of Godot's anti-aliasing options to try and eliminate the outliner's aliasing. The ones that wouldn't have as much of an impact on performance would be FXAA and SMAA.

Saw some performance issues with large selections and transforms so added a cache for outline instances that should help.

>I wonder if it would be a good idea to enable one of Godot's anti-aliasing options to try and eliminate the outliner's aliasing.

I'll defer to a rendering maintainer on what a good middle ground is for performance vs aesthetics for the engine.

Is it possible to make the outliner take into account materials with alpha testing or alpha hashing? From what I can see, it will be more difficult for the outline to consider materials with alpha blending, since they are not in the opaque pass, but I think it can at least be done for alpha testing or alpha hashing. Here are some images so you can better understand what I mean.

> I couldn't reproduce the mismatching active node after these changes so I suspect it may have been a timing issue due to the multiple calls. Let me know if it's still a problem and I can investigate further.

It's fixed now.

Something to consider. I usually split the view so I can activate the `Cinematic Preview` in one, which disables all gizmos for better visualization, while I edit in another. But the outline still renders in `Cinematic Preview`. It could be enabled/disabled per view in the top-left 3D view menu instead of a global setting.

> Is it possible to make the outliner take into account materials with alpha testing or alpha hashing?

This causes issues because 3D picking ignores texture transparency. The outline will be an imprecise representation of the actual geometry, making object selection difficult.

> This causes issues because 3D picking ignores texture transparency. The outline will be an imprecise representation of the actual geometry, making object selection difficult.

You're right, I thought this was only visual and that it would take the object's AABB to select.

Edit: I've taken a closer look at how Unity's outline behaves, and it can indeed take the transparency mask into account since the outline is drawn according to it, whether it's alpha testing or alpha blending. But here's something strange: when selecting the object, there's precision when using alpha testing, but it's very imprecise with alpha blending. So the question remains, will it be possible with the approach of this PR, at least with alpha testing?

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7a263f1-df8d-4875-b980-6a74b84196aa

>But the outline still renders in Cinematic Preview. It could be enabled/disabled per view in the top-left 3D view menu instead of a global setting.

This is fixed. I also tied the outline visibility to `View Gizmos` so they work the same way as the AABBs. The global setting is meant to just toggle between outlines and AABB.

I've addressed most the feedback above I believe:

I measured the same time for AABB and selection outline, no more crashes, scaling properly updates, and multiplying by `EDSCALE`.

Some exceptions:

>The outline is not affected by MSAA, screen-space AA or TAA/FSR2. I've tried to apply MSAA or SMAA to selection_buffer_viewport but it doesn't have intended effect, so I guess it would need additional shader changes to work.

Not quite sure how to address this, open to suggestions. Would this be a blocker for merging?

>The changes here should be implemented in the remote selection as well.

I'm personally not very familiar with the runtime portion of the codebase. Perhaps this can be a separate PR?
Are you suggesting we merge this regressing MSAA, screen-space AA or TAA/FSR2?

>Are you suggesting we merge this regressing MSAA, screen-space AA or TAA/FSR2?

I'm not sure it counts as a regression if it doesn't affect the main editor viewport. If I understand correctly, he's saying that it has no effect in the selection buffer viewport which only contains the outlines which is a separate thing and didn't exist before. This is also a togglable feature, so users do have the option of returning back to using the AABB which is unaffected. 

I wasn't asking for lack of intent to investigate a solution to this but to prioritize things since I use a fork of the Godot editor itself for a project, and like to properly schedule things for maintenance, get wider feedback and assistance. Apologies if it sounded like I was trying to get this out the door prematurely.

The same anti-aliasing as the regular render will not work well for a selection outline. You need to apply its own anti-aliasing method.

A method that antialias the transparent part so that the well-defined solid part is preserved. An option is an FXAA that runs on the alpha instead of the luminance/color.

> Not quite sure how to address this, open to suggestions. Would this be a blocker for merging?

I don't think so, this is still an improvement over what we have now.

What you could do is use SSAA by increasing `scaling_3d_scale` to `2.0` on the selection viewport. It would be relatively slow though, and would likely be better left disabled on mobile/web devices.
